findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany uses OR where the first branch is scoped to method SMS with past scheduledDate but the second branch is just retryCount gt 1 with no method or scheduled filter. That second branch will delete any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS) with retryCount > 1, even if scheduled true and due in the future. This is irreversible data loss and orphans provider jobs by deleting referenceId tracking. The retry branch must also filter method SMS and scheduled false.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment loses retries
findings.body: Both failure paths update with retryCount set to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value read when unscheduledReminders were fetched. If two cron invocations overlap, both read the same old value and both write the same new value, losing one retry. A perpetually failing number can then never reach gt 1 and will be retried forever. Use atomic retryCount increment instead of read-modify-write.

findings.title: Missing sendTo/message never increments retry
findings.body: When sendTo is falsy (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber) or message is empty, the guard around twilio.scheduleSMS is false and the code does no database update at all, leaving scheduled false and retryCount unchanged. The same reminder will be re-fetched on every cron run until its scheduledDate expires, and the same applies to the continue path when workflowStep or booking is missing. Since the PR goal is to stop endless rescheduling on invalid/missing numbers, these no-op paths must also increment retryCount or be cleaned up.
